name: Greenpaw Village
summary: Greenpaw Village lies between Raynewood Retreat and Silverwind Refuge, where the Foulweald furbolgs remain hostile. Chief Murgut and Shaman Oakpaw lead the corrupted tribe as Alliance and Horde forces clash with them in Ashenvale.

sections.title: A Corrupted Settlement
sections.body: South of Raynewood Retreat and northeast of Silverwind Refuge, Greenpaw Village holds the Foulweald furbolgs. Since the Third War, corruption in Ashenvale’s soil and spirits has tainted them. Chief Murgut leads the tribe, with Shaman Oakpaw as their corrupted spiritual guide. Travelers who enter their forest territory face attack.

sections.title: Caught in the Crosshairs
sections.body: The Foulweald’s attacks bring fighting to every side of Greenpaw Village. Alliance sentinels and night elf druids seek to purge the furbolgs and protect nearby outposts and sacred moonwells. Horde forces advancing through Ashenvale clash with them too, as both factions press through the woodland.

faq.answer: Greenpaw Village lies in central Ashenvale, south of Raynewood Retreat, northeast of Silverwind Refuge, and northwest of the southern moonwell.
The Foulweald furbolg tribe lives in Greenpaw Village. Chief Murgut leads them, with Shaman Oakpaw as their corrupted spiritual advisor.

faq.q: Why are the furbolgs in Greenpaw Village hostile?
faq.answer: Demonic corruption left after the Burning Legion invaded Ashenvale drove the Foulweald into maddened aggression.

faq.q: Why are the Alliance and Horde fighting here?
faq.answer: Both factions see the aggressive Foulweald as a threat to their roads and settlements. Night elves seek to cleanse or contain the madness near their moonwells, while Horde forces clash with the furbolgs as they advance through Ashenvale.

angles.text: For night elves, the Foulweald’s corruption near Raynewood Retreat and their sacred moonwells recalls Ashenvale’s lingering demonic scars.
As a druid, you witness the ancient bear folk’s pain at Greenpaw Village, where nature’s balance has broken into feral madness.
